newsitem.title: USA: SAFECO deal reflects consolidation pressure. [CORRECTED 22:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SAFECO deal reflects consolidation pressure. [CORRECTED 22:23 GMT]

text.p: SAFECO Corp's agreement to buy American States Financial Corp for a surprisingly high $2.8 billion reflects pressure facing U.S. property-casualty insurers to buy growth or end up being bought themselves.

"It indicates how rapidly it's consolidating where companies are getting to the point where they either have to be a buyer or a seller," Lehman analyst Peter Wade said. "And I suspect SAFECO didn't want to be a seller, so they needed to be a buyer."
SAFECO on Monday agreed to buy American States, 83.3 percent owned by Lincoln National Corp, for $47 a share, about a 23 percent premium to Friday's closing price.
"It's about as full a price as you can get," Salomon Brothers analyst Michael Smith said.
Most analysts had expected Lincoln National to get closer to $40 a share for its American States commercial property-casualty unit.
American States rose 7-1/4, or about 19 percent, to 45-3/8 in late trading. Lincoln National rose 3-1/4, or about five percent, to 66-1/8.
SAFECO shares fell 3/4, or about two percent, to 44-1/2, reflecting some of the concern about the price the company agreed to pay.
At $47 a share, SAFECO is paying about 2.2 times American States' book value, well above the levels paid for past property-casualty transactions, analysts said.
Although the price is steep, the deal will give SAFECO several strategic advantages, analysts said.

The deal will reduce the volatility of Seattle-based SAFECO's earnings by diversifying its business outside of the Northwest and lessening its dependence on its personal lines insurance business, Smith said.
American States, based in Indianapolis, is one of the largest writers of property and casualty insurance for small businesses.
The deal also puts SAFECO in a position to act as a consolidator in the property-casulaty industry, Lehman's Wade said.

The deal will enable SAFECO to "vault into a very strong market position in property-casualty, such that going forward they can potentially be a consolidator as opposed to lunch for one of the other consolidators," Wade said.
To be sure, the deal also carries some potential risks, Salomon's Smith said.
Although SAFECO said it expected the acquisition to contribute to earnings after 1998, Smith said he thought the company's projections might be too optimistic.
For SAFECO, the deal "depends on a lot of things going very right and nothing going very wrong in order for this to work from a financial standpoint," Smith said.
In addition, several rating agencies said they may cut SAFECO's debt ratings as a result of the transaction.
Moody's said it may lower SAFECO's AA3 senior long-term debt rating and Standard & Poor's said it may cut SAFECO's AA senior debt and corporate credit ratings.
Still, SAFECO's willingness to pay the price and take those risks shows that it is "really tough to grow" and that the "market is just that difficult," one analyst said.
"This is one high-priced bolt-on (acquisition)," he said.

And the fact that SAFECO was willing to pay that kind of a price and that American States apparently attracted a great deal of interest from potential buyers boosted the share prices of other property-casualty companies believed to be possible takeover targets.

Other companies believed to have expressed interest in American States included Hartford Financial Services Group, Germany's Allianz AG Holding, the U.K.'s General Accident Plc and Travelers Property Casualty Corp. Leveraged buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co also was believed to have teamed with USF&G Corp in making a bid.
"When you have an acquisition done at prices such as SAFECO is paying, it makes other properties that are known to be on the market that much more attractive," Smith said. (Corrects source).

Other shares moving higher on the American States acquisition included Ohio Casualty Corp, up 3-9/16, or nearly nine percent, to 43-1/4; USF&G Corp, up 1-1/8, or about five percent, to 23; and TIG Holdings Inc , up 3/4, or nearly three percent, to 28-7/8.
